study_identification_part.si4_title: Investigating dopaminergic abnormalities in schizophrenia and first-episode psychosis with normative modelling and multisite molecular neuroimaging

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states its objectives: to demonstrate feasibility of applying normative modelling (NM) to molecular neuroimaging (PET), extend striatal analyses to whole-brain, identify common patterns across independent psychosis datasets, link deviations to symptoms and treatment response, and evaluate prediction of treatment response.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: In this work, our primary objective is to demonstrate the feasibility of employing normative modelling for molecular neuroimaging in SCZ and psychotic disorders... we hypothesise that normative modelling can serve as a powerful tool to identify both the magnitude and the spatial distribution... by 1) extending analysis of dopamine alterations in the striatum to the whole brain, 2) identifying common patterns... and 3) linking inter-individual deviation from normalities to clinical symptoms and response to treatment. Lastly... we built a classifier to assess the value of [18F]FDOPA PET NM for predicting treatment response...

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study builds new NMs from existing healthy control (HC) datasets. It cites the original publications for data acquisition and reports scanner types and HC sample sizes (PHNO: PET/CT N=54, PET/MR N=23; FDOPA HC datasets totalling 142 HCs). However, explicit HC inclusion/exclusion criteria and image quality/missing-data standards are deferred to prior studies and not detailed here; reasons for exclusion are not reported.
